overview: Ingersoll Rand designs, manufactures, markets and services mission-critical air, gas, fluid, and specialty pumping and compression equipment, along with related aftermarket parts, consumables and services, under a multi-brand portfolio (Ingersoll Rand, Gardner Denver, Nash, ARO, Haskel, ILC Dover, Milton Roy and dozens of others). The company, headquartered in Davidson, North Carolina and formerly Gardner Denver Holdings before renaming in 2020 following its 2020 merger with the Ingersoll-Rand industrial segment, operates two segments: Industrial Technologies & Services (roughly 78-79% of revenue; air/gas compressors, vacuum and blower products, fluid transfer, power tools) and Precision & Science Technologies (roughly 21-22%; precision pumps, life-sciences fluid handling, and hydrogen/clean-energy components). It sells globally through direct sales and independent distributors to industrial, medical, water/wastewater, chemical processing, food & beverage, and clean-energy end markets.

business_model.summary: Ingersoll Rand generates revenue from original equipment sales (compressors, pumps, blowers, vacuum systems) plus a large and growing aftermarket business of parts, consumables and services that runs on the installed base independent of new-equipment cycles (aftermarket is roughly 35-40% of total revenue). Growth is driven organically through pricing, volume and a decentralized 'IRX' (Ingersoll Rand Execution Excellence) operating playbook, and inorganically through a high-velocity pipeline of bolt-on acquisitions (typically founder-owned niche players bought at ~9-10x pre-synergy EBITDA and re-rated toward mid-teens ROIC within about three years) plus occasional larger transformational deals (e.g., the $2.325B ILC Dover acquisition in 2024 that expanded the addressable market into life sciences). Q3 2026 orders accelerated sharply (consolidated orders +21% reported/+18% organic, book-to-bill >1.1x), partly on a large ~$195M long-cycle engineered-to-order win in Industrial Technologies & Services, signaling improving demand momentum entering 2027.

revenue_streams.name: Aftermarket parts, consumables & services (cuts across both segments)
New equipment / OEM (cuts across both segments)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - industrial manufacturers, medical/life-sciences device and biopharma customers, water/wastewater utilities, chemical processors, food & beverage producers, and clean-energy/hydrogen developers, sold via direct sales force and independent distributors
business_model.geographic_mix: Global manufacturing and sales footprint with meaningful exposure to the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific (including China); management has flagged China as a difficult pricing environment, with regional overcapacity pressuring local pricing though management describes the pressure as moderating

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest global players in air/gas compression, vacuum and blower equipment, and a growing niche leader in precision pumping and life-sciences fluid handling following the ILC Dover acquisition and subsequent bolt-ons (Scinomix, Fox S.r.l.); the broader compression/vacuum/blower marketplace remains highly fragmented across product technologies and channels rather than dominated by a single player

moat_factors.description: A large, aging installed base of compressors and pumps generates recurring, higher-margin parts and service revenue (roughly 35-40% of sales) that is stickier and less cyclical than new-equipment sales

moat_factors.factor: M&A platform and IRX operating system
moat_factors.description: A repeatable, disciplined process for sourcing proprietary (often founder-owned) bolt-on targets at attractive multiples and improving them through a standardized lean operating playbook (100-day sprints, weekly IMPACT Daily Management) is a differentiated, difficult-to-replicate capability compounding scale over time; FY2026 deals include Scinomix, Fox S.r.l./XF S.r.l., Lone Star Blower, and a US pump manufacturer closing October 30, 2026

Nine P&L leaders reporting to the CEO with ~60 sub-P&Ls underneath enables fast integration of acquisitions and close-to-customer decision-making versus more centralized industrial conglomerates; recent group-president promotions (Scott Watson, Shaun Carlson) as longtime executive Mike Weatherred prepares to retire keep this bench refreshed

Multi-brand strategy (Gardner Denver, Nash, ARO, Haskel, Milton Roy, ILC Dover, etc.) allows serving many fragmented niches without diluting individual brand equity, but no single brand carries category-defining pricing power comparable to a premium industrial leader
Products in life sciences and medical end markets require customer qualification cycles that create switching costs once designed into a validated process

weaknesses: Highly fragmented end markets with several large, well-capitalized competitors (Atlas Copco, Dover, IDEX) limit pricing power and market share gains through organic means alone

Organic growth has been volatile and historically weak (roughly a 1.4% average YoY decline over FY2024-FY2025) though it has recently inflected positive (4% organic revenue growth, 18% organic order growth in Q3 2026), leaving open the question of whether the improvement is durable or order-timing/large-project driven
Heavy reliance on continued acquisition volume to sustain growth narrative; any slowdown in deal flow or deterioration in acquired-company integration would expose softer organic trends
China pricing pressure from regional overcapacity has weighed on Industrial Technologies & Services underlying margins (down 120bps YoY in Q3 2026 excluding one-time tariff refunds)

The ILC Dover acquisition required a representation-and-warranty insurance claim after a post-close discovery of issues, resulting in $425.1M of gross recoveries from insurers/third parties recognized through 2026 - a reminder that even the disciplined M&A playbook carries diligence and integration risk on larger deals
No dominant, singular technological moat comparable to aerospace-grade certification businesses; competitive advantage rests more on execution and capital allocation than on hard-to-replicate IP

growth_drivers: Continued high-velocity bolt-on M&A pipeline - FY2026 deals include Scinomix (lab automation, ~10x pre-synergy EBITDA), Fox S.r.l./XF S.r.l. (metering/dosing), Lone Star Blower, Fai Filtri, and a US pump manufacturer acquisition closing October 30, 2026; board increased buyback authorization by $2 billion in Q3 2026, signaling capacity for continued capital deployment across M&A and buybacks

Order momentum re-acceleration - consolidated Q3 2026 orders of $2,345M were up 21% reported / 18% organic with book-to-bill above 1.1x in both segments, the strongest order print in several quarters, aided by a ~$195M long-cycle engineered-to-order win

Aftermarket/services mix shift - growing installed base (particularly boosted by ILC Dover and other recent life-sciences and precision-pump acquisitions) supports higher-margin, more resilient recurring revenue over time

Precision & Science Technologies momentum - Life Sciences orders and revenue each grew low-double-digits in Q3 2026, with segment adjusted EBITDA margin up 180-350bps YoY, continuing to outpace the legacy Industrial Technologies & Services segment

Clean-energy/hydrogen and water/wastewater secular demand - IR's precision pumping, hydrogen compression and dosing technologies are positioned for growth in clean-energy infrastructure and municipal water investment

Tariff/price pass-through and reshoring - company has managed an estimated ~$150-170M of 2026 tariff costs via pricing/surcharges and is realigning sourcing toward in-region supply chains, which could benefit from broader reshoring/industrial capex trends; IEEPA tariff refunds provided a one-time boost in Q3 2026

Deleveraging capacity for further M&A - net debt/adjusted EBITDA fell to 1.6x (down 0.2x YoY) with $3.9B of liquidity as of Q3 2026, and a large one-time ILC Dover litigation recovery (~$425M gross) further strengthened the balance sheet

business.description: Organic revenue was roughly flat-to-negative over FY2024-FY2025; Q3 2026 showed a sharp re-acceleration (4% organic revenue, 18% organic orders) partly driven by a large one-off long-cycle order, so it remains unclear how much reflects a genuine demand inflection versus lumpy project timing

Dozens of bolt-on deals plus larger transactions (ILC Dover for $2.325B) create ongoing integration execution risk; the ILC Dover R&W insurance claim ($425.1M gross recovery) illustrates that diligence/integration issues can surface even in deals structured with insurance protection

Regional overcapacity has pushed China pricing negative; Industrial Technologies & Services underlying margin was still down ~120bps YoY in Q3 2026 excluding one-time tariff refunds, indicating normalization remains a multi-period process
Numerous credible competitors (Atlas Copco, Dover, IDEX, Flowserve, Xylem) compete on product quality, efficiency, service and local presence, limiting structural pricing power

A DOJ False Claims Act matter involving ILC entities (predating IR's ownership, reportedly remediated within ~4 months of closing, no admission of wrongdoing) underscores the compliance risk that comes with acquiring numerous small/mid-size businesses

financial.description: Serial acquisition strategy is funded partly with debt, but net debt/adjusted EBITDA improved to 1.6x in Q3 2026 (down 0.2x YoY), giving more cushion than a year ago even as the board added $2B of buyback capacity

FY2026 guidance embeds ~$230M of net interest expense; a heavier acquisition pace funded with incremental debt in a higher-for-longer rate environment would pressure coverage and free cash flow available for buybacks/dividends
Meaningful non-US revenue and manufacturing base creates FX translation risk; FY2026 guidance embeds roughly a 1% currency tailwind that could reverse

Q3 2026 GAAP net income ($670M, $1.73/sh) and part of adjusted EBITDA/EPS were materially boosted by a $380M recovery of acquisition-related losses and IEEPA tariff refunds; investors need to track the company's own excl.-refund figures ($1.01 adjusted EPS vs. $1.07 headline) to assess underlying run-rate

regulatory.description: Company has been managing roughly $150-170M of gross tariff cost impact in 2026, working to offset via pricing/surcharges; incremental tariff escalation, reversal of IEEPA refunds, or an inability to pass through costs would compress margins
Manufacturing operations globally are subject to environmental and industrial safety regulation across multiple jurisdictions, with attendant compliance costs

ILC Dover and other precision/life-science products are subject to customer and regulatory (e.g., FDA-adjacent) qualification standards; failure to maintain qualifications could impair sales in that segment

macro.description: New-equipment orders are sensitive to global industrial production, capital spending cycles and manufacturing PMI; a broader industrial slowdown would pressure the larger Industrial Technologies & Services segment despite the recent order upturn
Slower China industrial activity and local overcapacity have produced negative pricing; a deeper China slowdown would be an incremental drag even as management frames it as gradually improving

Trades at a premium multiple relative to underlying organic growth; analyst consensus targets cluster in the low-to-mid $90s (Street high ~$115) against a share price that has traded roughly in the $75-85 range in late 2026, implying the market is pricing meaningful continued execution on both organic recovery and M&A
Broader US trade policy shifts (beyond the currently modeled impact) could alter input costs, supply chains and end-customer capex decisions across IR's global footprint

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global industrial compression, vacuum, blower and precision fluid-handling markets are growing at low-to-mid single digit rates, supported by secular demand in life sciences/biopharma, clean energy (hydrogen), water/wastewater infrastructure and general industrial reshoring; Q3 2026 order data (book-to-bill >1.1x, organic orders +18%) suggests the near-term demand backdrop has improved versus the soft patch of 2024-2025, though China overcapacity/pricing pressure persists
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical - Industrial Technologies & Services (new equipment) tracks industrial capex and manufacturing activity, while the aftermarket business and Precision & Science Technologies (life sciences, precision pumps) are comparatively more resilient and less tied to the capex cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - direct balance sheet impact is manageable given improving leverage (~1.6x net debt/adjusted EBITDA as of Q3 2026), but a heavy reliance on continued M&A funding makes the cost and availability of debt capital relevant to the growth algorithm, and the premium equity multiple is vulnerable to rate-driven compression

recent_developments.event: Reported Q3 2026 results: revenue of $2,065M (+6% reported, +4% organic) and orders of $2,345M (+21% reported, +18% organic, book-to-bill 1.14x) both beat consensus comfortably; GAAP net income of $670M ($1.73/sh diluted) was boosted by a $380M recovery of acquisition-related losses tied to the ILC Dover R&W insurance claim; adjusted EPS of $1.07 (+24% YoY) beat the ~$0.88-0.90 consensus, though adjusted EPS excluding IEEPA tariff refunds was $1.01 (+17%)

Raised FY2026 guidance: revenue growth to 5.5%-7.0% (from 4.5%-6.5%), implying organic growth of 2-3.5% (up from 1-3%); adjusted EPS (excl. Q3 IEEPA refunds) raised to $3.58-$3.70 (from $3.45-$3.57); adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.13-$2.19B maintained, excluding the Q3 tariff refunds

Board authorized an additional $2 billion for share buybacks (on top of $313M remaining); Q3 2026 capital deployment included $350M of buybacks, $90M of M&A and $8M of dividends; net debt/adjusted EBITDA improved to 1.6x (down 0.2x YoY) with $3.9B of total liquidity

Announced/closed additional bolt-on M&A: Lone Star Blower (closed August 2026) and a US-based pump manufacturer expected to close October 30, 2026, continuing the high-velocity acquisition cadence alongside earlier-2026 deals Scinomix (life-sciences lab automation, January 2026, ~10x pre-synergy EBITDA) and Fox S.r.l./XF S.r.l. (metering and dosing, May 2026)

Recognized the bulk of a ~$425.1M gross insurance/third-party recovery tied to the ILC Dover acquisition (R&W claim for a post-close discovery of issues predating IR's ownership); $25.0M collected in Q2 2026 and $162.5M in Q3 2026, with the remainder expected in Q4 2026; a related DOJ False Claims Act matter involving legacy ILC entities was also resolved with IR stating the underlying compliance gaps predated its ownership and were remediated within approximately four months of closing

Segment detail: Industrial Technologies & Services revenue of $1,620M (+5% reported, +4% organic), orders $1,898M (+25% reported, +22% organic, book-to-bill 1.17x, aided by a ~$195M long-cycle engineered-to-order win); adjusted EBITDA margin 29.4% reported (+40bps YoY) but 27.8% excluding tariff refunds (-120bps YoY) on continued China pricing and inflation pressure. Precision & Science Technologies revenue of $445M (+7% reported, +6% organic), orders $448M (+7% reported, +4% organic, book-to-bill 1.01x); adjusted EBITDA margin 34.3% reported (+350bps) / 32.6% excluding refunds (+180bps); Life Sciences orders and revenue each grew low-double-digits

Leadership changes: CFO transition to Vikram Kini (succeeding Emily Weaver); group president roles expanded for Scott Watson and Shaun Carlson, reporting to Chairman/CEO Vicente Reynal, as longtime executive Mike Weatherred prepares to retire; former Tesla president Jerome Guillen joined the board effective January 1, 2026

Stock traded roughly in the $70s-$80s through much of H2 2026, well below its 52-week high near $101 (set February 2026) but above its 52-week low near $68; analyst consensus is Moderate Buy/Buy with mean price targets clustering in the low-to-mid $90s (Street-high views near $115) following the Q3 beat and raised guidance; Stifel upgraded to Buy with a $101 target in August 2026 and Citi has maintained a Buy rating with a target in the low-$100s

Held at the same level as Q2 guidance despite the revenue raise, reflecting continued China pricing and inflation pressure on margins
Raised from $3.45-$3.57; reflects lower net interest expense from improved leverage and the stronger order book, not the one-time tariff-refund benefit

items.target: Continued bolt-on cadence (US pump manufacturer closing Oct 30, 2026) plus an incremental $2 billion buyback authorization
items.notes: CEO described capital allocation strategy as 'led by M&A,' with buybacks as a complementary lever given improved leverage (1.6x net debt/adjusted EBITDA)

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Vicente Reynal cited an 'improved demand environment' with 'healthy short-to-medium cycle and long cycle business activity' underpinning the stronger Q3 2026 order book and the guidance raise. Management continues to frame Precision & Science Technologies (particularly Life Sciences) as the faster-growing, higher-margin growth engine, while characterizing China pricing softness as gradually normalizing rather than structurally impaired. The company treats the ~$425M ILC Dover-related insurance recovery and the Q3 IEEPA tariff refunds as non-recurring items excluded from its underlying adjusted guidance, directing investors to the ex-refund EPS figures ($1.01 in Q3, $3.58-$3.70 for FY2026) as the better read of run-rate earnings power.

bull_case: Order momentum has clearly re-accelerated - Q3 2026 consolidated orders up 21% reported/18% organic with book-to-bill above 1.1x in both segments - suggesting the two-year organic growth malaise may be inflecting positively heading into 2027

Proven, repeatable bolt-on M&A engine (IRX operating system) continues at pace (Scinomix, Fox S.r.l./XF S.r.l., Lone Star Blower, a pump manufacturer closing Oct 30 2026) with a disciplined ~9-10x pre-synergy entry multiple, and improved leverage (1.6x net debt/EBITDA) plus a fresh $2B buyback authorization give management more capital-allocation flexibility

Growing aftermarket/recurring revenue base (~35-40% of sales) and increasing mix shift toward higher-margin Precision & Science Technologies (Life Sciences orders/revenue up low-double-digits, margins up 180-350bps YoY in Q3 2026) improve earnings quality and resilience versus a pure industrial-cyclical peer

The ~$425M gross ILC Dover insurance recovery demonstrates management successfully protected shareholders from a post-close diligence issue via R&W insurance, converting what could have been a permanent value destroyer into a cash inflow that strengthened the balance sheet

Analyst sentiment has turned more constructive post-Q3 (Stifel Buy/$101, Citi Buy, consensus mean targets in the low-to-mid $90s), with the Q3 beat-and-raise providing a positive catalyst after a soft 2026 stock performance
bear_case: The Q3 2026 organic order surge was partly driven by a single ~$195M long-cycle engineered-to-order win in Industrial Technologies & Services, raising the question of whether the acceleration is a genuine demand inflection or lumpy project timing that will not repeat

Underlying (ex-tariff-refund) margins in the largest segment, Industrial Technologies & Services, were still down 120bps YoY in Q3 2026 on China pricing and inflation - the 'timing issue' management describes in China has now persisted for well over a year

A meaningful portion of Q3 2026's headline beat came from non-recurring items (a $380M ILC Dover litigation recovery and IEEPA tariff refunds); stripping these out, adjusted EPS growth of 17% is still solid but notably lower than the 24% headline figure, and investors must track management's own ex-refund guidance to avoid overstating run-rate earnings power

Continued reliance on debt-funded serial acquisitions carries real integration and diligence risk - the ILC Dover R&W claim, while resolved favorably, is a reminder that even transformational deals can surface unexpected post-close issues, including a related DOJ compliance matter

Stock has underperformed for much of 2026 (trading well below its ~$101 February 2026 high for most of H2) despite the Q3 beat, suggesting the market remains skeptical of the durability of both the organic re-acceleration and the premium multiple the M&A-driven growth algorithm commands
